t: Find Rolf Lisping on the surface and escort him back to the Lisping Family in the Rebel Refuge.

Horrible, ain't it? Thomething like that happenth every other day here. First the cultists, now the metal beasts. Ath far ath the howl of wind and the grinding of rusty metal... that never stopth. Maketh one think fondly of his thervice on Eljune. All the trouble we had there wath orc raids. Now the orcth and uth relieve each other on duty.
We were on patrol when those bladeth attacked. In the heat of battle, we lost our little brother Rolf! Had he been killed, he would have rithen already. Which meanth he's either wounded or unconscious. He didn't rethpond to our shouts... And we're thcared to keep shouting - the cultists might hear. Look for him, will you? He couldn't have gone far.
What if the cultists got him and are thucking out hith Thpark? Holy cow! We need to thpeed up our thearch!
Rolf, brother Rolfie, where have you been? They worked him over all right - look at that bump. If it weren't for you, he would have laid there until the cultists appeared. Thankth!
Somebody, help me! Thank the Light, you found me before Tep's servants did! Please help me return to the refuge. I hope my brothers are alive...
Attach detonators to the four mines on the bridges and report to Artem Sonin in the Rebel Refuge.

Rolf, brother, hang on! We're taking you to the doctor. The doctor's good, he's gonna mend you... Aw, our headth are like a thieve! We got a mission to complete! But we can't be in two placeth at once! Oh...
Excuthe uth, we're terribly ashamed of athking you to do our job for uth, but you thee Rolf's condition. Our headquarters' order ith: mine the bridgeth leading to the neighboring islands. The mineth are deployed, what's left to do ith attach detonators. Can you do it? We'll thank you for it later, honest! And we're gonna thee a doctor. Good luck!
Rolf, Rolf, however did that happen to you? Hang on a bit, the doctor ith gonna help...

Your courageous actions are an example for...
Oh, here I am talking like an Imperial officer again. There are no subjects of the Empire or the League here - we're all brothers and sisters. So I'll put it simply: thank you for saving this fluffy skin of Rolf. It goes double for repelling the attack on the Refuge!
Use the sarcophagus to enter illusion.

I've attached the crystals. It works! We can now connect to the sarcophagus without fear of it sucking out your Spark. The road to the illusory world is open - before Tep knows it, we'll destroy his network from within! But first you should practice being conscious of yourself in the world of dreams: the last thing you want is to get back into illusion only to become its prisoner again. I've created a small imaginary space - our own tiny illusory world. Let's get in the sarcophaguses and I'll show you what is what there how things are there. My assistants will observe our bodies - just to make sure there are no health risks. You coming?
What is reality? That depends on how you define that concept. If reality is what you can see, touch or taste, then everything around us is absolutely real.
We're here. Sorry for the lack of furnishings - I have better things to do than create illusory beauty.
Defeat the opponents summoned by Charles de Doucer and get back to the real world.

So, we're in our small illusory world. Let's call it Planar Rim, a place non-existent on the real Irdrich or on the illusory one, but one that grants access to both. Here, we can create anything we may need: illusory furniture, clothes, weapons, and even simulated opponents. That's what we're gonna do.
I'll summon a few enemies one by one. You have to defeat them. Meanwhile in the real world, my assistants will read the sensors and make sure the simulation does you no harm. If anything goes wrong, we'll try to get you out. Get ready for battle and tell me when to begin.
Be careful: these illusions cause pain that's quite real.
Welcome back to reality. Let's see what our sensors showed.
Greetings! I'd bid you good day, but that's an unaffordable luxury under the circumstances.
Collect 6 Power Crystals from the distribution devices on the Isle of Perils and bring them to Charles de Doucer in the Refuge.

Captives of the illusory world are sleeping in their sarcophaguses and dreaming of the green Irdrich. The longer they lie there, the more energy their Sparks give to Tep. To be defeated in the real world, Tep must be deprived of his supplies, disconnected from the illusory world. To do that, we need to get there somehow. Not as victims, but on our own terms.
The Resistance has got a broken sarcophagus, and I was able to fix and reconfigure it. However, if you get inside it now, it will feed on the light of your Spark. An alternative power supply is needed. Luckily, there is one. There used to be a lab on the isle we now call the Isle of Perils. Tep used to conduct his first experiments with sarcophaguses there. Early models were not very efficient, so they fed on the power crystals. Those crystal are very likely to still be there.
The only problem is: how do we get them? You see, the early version of the system failed, and all of the test subjects went insane. They destroyed the lab, slaughtered the scientists and smashed the equipment... The lab was closed and forgotten, but those wretched souls still wander around the isle - even death could not stop their madness. They pounce on everything they see. Be careful!
Tep promises power, glory and immortality, but all he gives is madness and death. What a moron I was to trust him!
You can now enter the illusion and retain your memory, consciousness and willpower. This gives us a fighting chance!
Kill 12 Sparkless Ones on the Isle of Perils and report to Charles de Doucer.

Do you know how Tep controls his cultists? First, he promises them the whole world, eternal life and a pair of ice skates on top of that. Then he charges an entrance fee and levies a monthly tax - the light of their Sparks. Though a hefty price, the neophyte agrees, for he's been promised much more. Finally, the newbie is sent recruiting other wretched souls. If you enlist another fool into the cult, you get a sip of his life. If you violate the rules, you pay with your own. That's what Tep's Pyramid is. Only its master and a handful of his minions profit from it. Some manage to accumulate a certain amount of other Sparks' light to make up for their losses and maintain a semblance of human existence. Those who are unlucky roam the ruins of Tep's kingdom with their Sparks faded. Glance around and you'll see what their souls look like.
Death is a merciful respite for those poor fools. Whatever they did in their lives, no one deserves that fate. Do them this last favor, help their faded Sparks rest in peace.
It looks like madness from the outside, but inside the cult keeps a stronger hold on you than psi-salt.
Finally, those seeking eternal life have found their peace. However, I fear that as long as fools exist, all sorts of cults will continue to prosper across the entire Sarnaut.
Fight Skeleton Warriors on the Isle of Perils to obtain 10 portions of Bone Flour and bring them to Pin the Crafty at the Rebel Refuge.

Are you hungry? Me too. Everyone is. There's no food, though. These dead rocks don't even yield wilted grass, and instead of mice we got metal crabs hopping around. You can always chew some dust, though, he he.
No fear! Our nerds found a solution. The Elves found some dried mushrooms and the Arisen managed to grow them without any soil, right on some racks. They taste like clay with garlic, but they're edible. All we need is water and fertilizer. The water supply is enough so far, but the fertilizer is running out, we need some more. The best fertilizer is bone flour. So go to the Isle of Perils, where you'll find appropriate skeletons. Crush a dozen and bring me what is left of them. And don't think too much about that when you eat the mushrooms, he he he!
You'll do much more than that when you're hungry! Or get back into illusion with your happy meals and frappuccinos!
Yeah, that's good. I'll grind it a bit more finely and feed the mushrooms. We won't stay hungry. Though we won't be full, either, he he.
Explore the ruins on the Isle of Perils and report to Klavdia Kalugina at the Refuge.

This is just too good: gods and challengers for divine power tearing each other apart! You can laugh your ass off. Of course, we won't be laughing long. Sarn is yelping somewhere under a bench licking his wounds, and my dear father ran off. Who's next in line to become the master of Sarnaut? His rotten majesty, Tep! You can't even imagine how many Sparks he swallowed. He's one step away from being a deity. And the entire Sarnaut will turn into a vast cemetery. There's only one power that can stop him now - the likes that made my dear father flee. The likes of you.
I bet on you, heroes. By the way, if you wonder whom you should thank for getting out of the sarcophaguses in the first place, I am at your service. You can also thank me for the fact that the Resistance has not yet been found and exterminated... Or did you think Tep suddenly grew short-sighted?
Never mind, enough chit-chat, let's get down to business. There are some very interesting ruins on the Isle of Perils. I don't know who built them or who destroyed them, but I think they were there long before Tep appeared. Take a walk to the ruins and see if you can get inside. If you can, report back. And if you can't, find out why.
Onward, you brave pawn! The last rank is yet so far away!

Lictors! Those are Tep's select servants, his elite guards. They don't guard ordinary rocks. Tep surely keeps something interesting in that tower. But the wall... Never mind, there are more important matters for now. We'll have time to look for an entrance later.
Fight Sparkless Ones on the Isle of Perils to obtain 15 Arrows of the Forester Tribe and bring them back to Puff the Forester.

Hey you, stop! Come here! Don't be scared, I won't touch you. There's a problem.
It goes like this. I was walking around the island with the dead when I ran into a whole mob. I shot them full of holes, but my arrows just don't take them down. They pierce them but do no harm. So I made a dash for it. It took me some time to realize that I'd used up both the ordinary arrows and the carved ones that belonged to our clan. I hate to leave them in this mess among the corpses. But I can't get them back, seeing as my weapon is useless against the enemy. Will you bring them back? I'll owe you a drink.
Scared to go to an isle swarming with the dead, eh?
Oh, that's fine! They're my babies. Here, take this.
Kill Fatass, an orc zombie on the Isle of Perils, and report to Puff the Forester.

Here's the deal. Apart from the dead, there's an orc walking around on the Isle of Perils. Big and mean and with a fat ass. Tep decorated him all right. With cables all over, an urn for a head, hands and feet in shackles and some wires sticking out his ass, he looks worse than our very own Zem. Don't know which clan he belongs to, but I was scared witless once I saw him. He walks around the ruins mumbling something... Man, is that the way an orc should die? It's a shame - his ancestors must be choking on tears and snot in the afterworld.
Listen, if you ain't scared, find and finish off the poor bastard. Better to croak in battle than walk around like that and go foul. Keep in mind, though: he's a big fella, you won't take him down in a fair fight. Get some tough guys to help you beat the crap out of him. And I'll give you a nice reward. We have a deal?
An orc zombie, imagine that! I can't frigging believe it, seven hells!
He done for? May he rest in peace, man. He may have been a cultist, but I wouldn't wish that sort of death on the biggest asshole. Here, take it as promised.
Use the Spear of Truth to pierce the illusory wall on the Isle of Perils. Take care of the guards and use the brooch to summon Klavdia and report your success to her.

OK, let's play ghost busters at a later time. Now, let's see how good this spear is in the real world. Remember the flickering wall that prevented us from exploring the ruins? I think this spear will be of greater help than a hundred-ton battering ram.
Go to the wall and try piercing it with the spear. I reckon there should be no problem this time. Take my brooch. If you manage to make a breach in the wall, rub the stone. I'll teleport to you and we'll decide what to do next.
I wonder if we draw too much attention to us by using this artifact from the illusory world...
Did it work? That's what I thought. Excellent! And now... You like sticking your nose where it doesn't belong? I, for one, live for it. So that's what we're gonna do.
Obtain 5 Astral Mines from the crates on the shipwreck. Use the brooch to summon Klavdia Kalugina and give the mines to her.

OK, let's finish our exciting journey into the past and get back to our problems in the real world. The cultists we'd driven away from the tower ruins complained to their master, and he sent a strike force against us. Luckily, the punishers have to overcome piles of garbage to get here, so we have some time to prepare a surprise for them.
One of the Imperial ships had explosives in its hold. Miraculously, they survived the shipwreck, and now they will come in handy. Inspect the ship's frame carefully, collect some five mines and call me to find out the details of our sophisticated plan.
If you crack a joke about a warm welcome, you'll disappoint me greatly.
Take a look: good as new! Glory to Imperial science: whilst the mechanism is not loaded, you can play goblinball with them.
Open the safe and bring its contents to Gleb Partisanov.

Sh... They're not here? Quiet, they may hear us!
Where are you from? I thought none of ours was alive! Those who didn't die in the crash were taken by those... things. Are you sure one of them isn't around? We need to be careful, or they may take us too!
What? The Resistance? Holy moly, then why am I sitting here, afraid to stick my nose outside? Thank you! I'll hurry over to our guys.
Wait, wait, I almost forgot. When they came, they took both the living and the dead, ripped everything of value off the ship, but failed to open the captain's safe. They're still hanging around trying to crack it, but nuts to them: it's made in the Empire! Don't know what's in there, but I'm sure it's not some trash. I've kept the key, take it. See you in the Refuge!
A captain's safe? You wouldn't put unimportant stuff in there. Now, run to the ship as fast as you can, before the cultists get hold of the contents!
What's this document? Let me have a look. Looks like it's written in Xadaganian... Leave it, I'll try to crack it later.
Deploy an astral mine, lead Tep's punishers to it and activate the charge.

Tep's punishers are nearing, but we have all we need. Take this astral mine - you'll have to use it as an anti-personnel device. Here's the plan. First, deploy the bomb in the ship's frame. I'm setting the timer at... Would fifteen seconds be enough for you to get out of there? Good. Then the next step is: when the punishers show up on the bridge, draw their attention and lead them inside the ship. Then press this button on the mine and run like hell. In an enclosed space, an explosion that strong will tear them to shreds and if you don't move your ass, you'll join them. Don't you dare die in there! I have a lot more plans for you.
What're you waiting for? The punishers are just about to get here!

Do you have any idea how lucky you were? Surviving the manual activation of a mine with a defective timer takes much more than being born with a silver spoon in your mouth - we're talking at least a set of platinum tableware! When Klavdia told me what had happened, we rushed to dig out the fragments of the ship. We thought we'd be lucky if we found anything to bury. So what did we find? Tep's servants were reduced to a pulp, but you were just stunned without a scratch on you. You're protected by someone above, I'm telling you.
Fight the cultists in the Tower Ruins to obtain 20 Cultist's Notepads. Summon Klavdia by using the brooch and give them to her.

Just take a look! These stones... You can't confuse this architecture with anything. Long ago, maybe even before the Cataclysm, this was the site of a Great Mage's tower. A tidbit for any sorcerer! It may have rotted and dried up over the centuries, but Tep still clung to it with all the teeth he had left. Here, any old rock can hide a mystery!
And here come the researchers. A whole archeological expedition - enough to make the Historians jealous. We have no time for excavations, so we'll use the fruits of their toil. Drive away the cultists and take their notes. Meanwhile, I'll go back to the Refuge to stay out of sight. You still have the brooch with you? That's good. Call me when you're through.
They may find it difficult to dig with sickles. But you'll do much more than that for the divine leader!

Unbelievable. Reading these essays, you would think the authors were smart. But when you realize that these same brainiacs are now hopping around on rocks barefoot with nothing but undergarments and hoods on...
Destroy 20 Research Probes in the Tower Ruins and report to Artem Sonin.

Tep values his mechanical toys much more than all of his fanatics who worship him. Look at those flying saucers. All lubricated, each blade sharpened, each screw polished - a feast for the eyes! Not like those goners in baggy rags. To him, they're nothing but cheap labor and - at a later time - food. I can't say I feel sorry for them - who's to blame for their joining the cult by free choice? But my hands are itching to spoil their master's pleasure. Why don't we break Tep's favorite toys? This way we'll also suspend the diggings - two birds with one stone! If there are any secrets left in the tower, they're not for Tep to know.
An interesting question: do the cultists happen to grease Tep's mechanisms with their own fat instead of engine oil? That's unlikely, but it wouldn't surprise me. They're so damn skinny.
What used to be machines is now junk. While they're being fixed, we'll proceed with the diggings.
Go down to the Tower Ruins cellar and explore the anomaly.

I looked through the cultists' notes as long as I could make out the handwriting. It wasn't in vain that we drove them away. Judging by the notes, the owner of this tower experimented with magical energies and found a source of unparalleled power. One of the experiments was especially lucky - it razed the tower to the ground. And because that was long ago, even before the Divine Gift, no one ever heard of the mage since.
Of course, Tep won't learn from others' mistakes as he craves the same source of energy. His minions are rummaging through the ruins trying to grasp what his experiments were all about. They've found no notes, artifacts, or operational machines for now. The tower cellar, however, hides an energy anomaly that somehow influences the flow of time. What it is remains unclear, as it aggressively resists any attempts to research it. The text is illegible and the edges of the notepad are burnt. Interesting, isn't it? It is to me, for instance. Still, it's you who will go there.
Welcome to my tower. I did tell you we'd soon meet again. Don't you recognize me? Well, I guess that's to be expected... I am, after all, a Ghost.

Yes, I'm the Ghost. That's not a nickname, though, but rather my current state, if you will. Please excuse me for mystifying it, but I wouldn't like to be prematurely spotted by someone you know. I don't want to be rude, but that lady is very, very dangerous. I can't tell for sure who she is, but I don't trust her in the least. And neither should you.
So, now that we're alone, I can let you into the matter without fear. I must warn you: this is a long story. How should I begin...
Centuries can't be squeezed into a short story. While we're here, though, we have plenty of time.

In the real world, I'm still an invisible shadow bound by the time standing still. However, the illusory world is beyond reality, and I have some freedom in it. I helped you make a spear that, in turn, led you to me. The time has come for the last phase of my plan, so to speak.

Most of all, I crave to break free from this tower that became both my prison and my grave for many years. Alas, I am but an incorporeal shadow, and my only power is knowledge. That was enough to bring you here, but there is no way I can make you believe, let alone help me. All I can do is humbly ask for your help until you agree. Fortunately, I have time to convince you: no one but me can help you get back to the real world. Likewise, no one but you can help me. So, do we have a deal? Great. If so, let's waste no time.
First of all, we need to take care of my disciples. As you can see, I made it through the years of imprisonment tolerably, but my disciples were not so strong of spirit. They lost their minds and now they're wandering around the ruins, gripped by merciful madness. The time has come to bring them back to reality, though.
Fortunately, they are easier to heal than living madmen. First, you need to attract the ghost's attention. Alas, the only way to do this is to hurt him: slap him on the cheeks, punch him, burn him with a spell... Don't worry: you can't inflict any serious injury in this place, where the time is frozen. As soon as the ghost turns his attention to you, just call him out. They haven't heard voices of the living beings for centuries, and this will surely enliven them.
Get back to me when seven of my disciples restore their minds, so to speak.
At times, I'd also dream about diving into the same depths of madness. It was only through crazy, unrealizable hope that I managed to stay sane. And here it is, my hope come true.
Insanity is a horrible state. Though sometimes it's better to be insane than to see the world going mad with no chance to remedy it...

Get back to the real world. Use the ritual knife to summon Astral Skinners with the smell of your blood. Fight them to obtain 5 portions of Demon's Ashes and bring those to the Ghost in the Frozen Time.

Now we're going to need something that can't be found in the frozen time. Energy? What was that? Oh no, thank you for your generous offer, but mana batteries can't help us. We need something better assimilable, more volatile. Alas, I can't ask you to simply draw a bucketful of Astral and bring it here... Wait, that's actually a good idea! Some fresh astral demon ashes is what we need. It doesn't contain much energy, but it's enough for our purpose and - most importantly - it's easy to consume.
Yes, I know there are no demons on Irdrich. No problem: there's an easy way to lure them. You already guessed what I'm talking about, right? Take this knife. Spill a few drops of your blood in the Astral, and someone of their damned breed will come rushing to the smell. Five handfuls of their ashes will be more than enough. I look forward to your return.
As you see, even demons can be of help in certain cases.
What a wonderful feeling. Here where time is frozen, the energy is pure like a breeze in a musty storeroom. Everything is ready for the ritual - so, with your permission, let's begin!
Hold the ritual that will free the Ghost and his disciples.

We're set. Can it... Can it finally... Please forgive the old man, I can't control my feelings. Who'd ever thought that an incorporeal ghost could have his hands shaking?
Please help me this last time by taking part in the ritual. Don't worry: you don't have to learn magic in detail. My disciples and I will do everything by ourselves. All you need to do is follow my instructions in a timely manner.
I will teach you three Words of a very, very old language. The first is the Word of Power, the second the Word of Strength, the third the Word of Death. When the ritual begins, we'll start casting a spell and you'll have to weave these Words into the spell one by one, figuratively speaking. I'll make a sign for you to speak each of the Words. Don't worry if you make a mistake: if the first attempt fails, we can repeat the ritual. Are you ready?
Stay focused or you'll have to start from scratch!

That's it. Now that my disciples are finally free, I'll follow them. Surprised? You thought I had hoped to rise only for another shot at the gods? No, my friend, I haven't lost my mind, unlike the current owner of Irdrich. All these centuries I've been dreaming about peace, not revenge. You know, I did a lot of evil to my poor Sarnaut already... However, that's not for you to know. I'm taking my guilt with me. What I ask of you is: burn the cultists' notes on my experiment for your own good. It failed and brought about nothing but grief. Forget about all you've seen here. Forget about me, too.
No worries, let's try it again. Here, we can repeat our attempts endlessly.
Go back to the real world and relate the Ghost's words to Klavdia.

Before I leave you forever, allow me to tell you something. I've watched the illusory world since its conception. This is not a mere mirage. It's alive, and it's greater, stronger and more beautiful than its creator. The imaginary Irdrich will survive without a master while the dream architect himself will weaken unspeakably without it. And I can give you a hint on how to end his tyranny.
Any spell has its core, so to speak. The world of dreams does as well. That must be some critical spot for this world. I thought the core was in the Cave of Elements, but I was wrong, as you can see. Free the core of illusion from its architect's control, and you'll free the entire Irdrich - first the illusory and then perhaps even the real one. Relate this to all your allies, including the dame we both know.
That is all. Farewell, my friend. Good luck on your path: I'm afraid this ancient evil won't leave the pages of history as peacefully as I am.

That's some story! I wish I could have talked to him. You're surprising me, though: releasing the ghost of an ancient mage without guarantee or anything. Good thing he proved peaceful. What if he hadn't? He even had a fresh body at hand that was willing to take part in some obscure rituals! What if he'd gotten inside you and we'd had another Tep? Maybe that's what he did, eh? Come, tell me where we first met! Eh?!
Right, on the Coba Plateau. All right, then, may he rest in peace. As to his advice... We can surely look for that core of illusion, but I wouldn't be too hopeful if I were you. I don't have much trust in the information from a suicidal fossil.
Kill two sentries at the Final Redoubt, deploy the bomb next to the battery control console, and use the flare to signal to Brawler the Fierce.

Our struggle is entering the decisive stage. The main enemy forces moved inside the Pyramid, leaving only small garrisons outside. We have a chance to penetrate into Tep's stronghold and take care of him once and for all. This is our final and decisive battle!
There's only one obstacle that separates us from the Pyramid: a tiny, but seriously fortified isle. Attacking it head-on is suicide: the guns will pulverize us in seconds. The only way out is another guerilla operation. Seeing as you're experienced, you'll do it.
Here's the plan. Sneak up to the redoubt walls without the enemy noticing you and kill the guards. Then sneak inside and deploy this bomb next to the turret control console. Finally, make sure the battery is disabled and use this flare to signal to our squad. The squad will be led by a vet named Brawler the Fierce - a proven and reliable warrior. Then proceed according to the circumstances. Any questions? No questions. Then get started!
Holy cow! This is the first time I have had to command... err... gibberlings! They're tough fighters, albeit undisciplined. Well, the same could be said about ours.
Nicely done. Now my boys will capture the fortification in an instant!
Aided by the rebels, destroy the three Pyramid Keepers and use the flare to give a signal to the Resistance.

The boys are ready and eager to engage. We seem to be planning a kind of Astral Campaign: the orcs, the elves and the gibberlings are all armed to the teeth and their hands are itching to bring down the Pyramid. Now we need to lay a path inside. We'll have to remove those gilded wood lice, Tep's elite guards. Don't be scared: we'll all attack together at once - and stomp them! Once you finish them, use the flare to give a signal to the rest of the troops. Victory's in the bag! Boy, is Tep going to get it, he he!
Let's raze the Pyramid to the ground!
Rush into the Pyramid and fight Tep

The way is clear! The old bastard is trembling in his bunker, but he has an hour to live, if that. I hope he won't have time to swallow some poison capsule: lots of ours would like to finish him personally. What're we waiting for? Let's roll! Let's crush the spider in his lair!
Rush into the Pyramid and fight Tep? Head-on, just like that? Are you nuts?

Tep grabbed your boys by the neck and used them as cleaning rags, didn't he? Oh, this should be good! Did you expect to find a skinny old man, cuff him and take him to the capital for a fair trial? Hello! This is Tep! To him, Sparks are a snack and genocide is entertainment on boring nights! All we did so far only caused him some inconvenience - nothing more!
Now don't start panicking. He can be defeated, or I wouldn't be talking to you now. You know why he let you go? He wants to play cat-and-mouse with you. Tep doesn't even think the Resistance poses any threat to him. His presumption will ruin him... If yours doesn't kill you first, of course.
Collect 10 hearts from the energy elementals at the Western Outpost, use them to make a mana-bomb and place it under the mechanoid plant. Report back to Gleb Patrisanov in the Refuge.

In order not to let this tragedy happen again, we will act with caution. Our plan is to deprive Tep of his resources, forcing him to barricade himself in the Pyramid, then... Then we'll see. Now that he lost his main source of energy, the next step is to destroy the plant producing mechanoids.
Initially we thought it would stop without power, but the cultists came over us. They had a back-up power source, magic elementals. Well, we'll use the magic spirits that revived the production line to stop it forever.
The matter is that those elementals are very unstable, thus you won't even need to use a bomb or something of that kind. Just kill a dozen of elementals and put their hearts together. Ten hearts is like a critical mass. When they are combined and left for some time, they always explode better than a torpedo. Be sure to run away quick, as soon as you put them under the production line!
How great it could have been, to defeat Tep by sudden attack... Well, let's start a siege.
Wow, what a blow! This plant won't start working any time soon!
Kill 12 Technicians and Chief Engineer at the Western Outpost. Report back to Gleb Partisanov in the Refuge.

Gathering all this force in the Pyramid, Tep has left only a small garrison and a dozen of workers at the plant. They will become our last target. Go to the Western Outpost, to the mechanoid plant, and kill everyone who is still working there. Be sure to find and defeat the Chief Engineer, too!
It's a pity that all those clever people agreed to serve Tep in his war against life itself. They could have stayed at home and serve the war between the League and the Empire... Oh, forget it.
Tep has sent them to their doom, a silly death without any chance to be resurrected. I'm sure they knew it, and yet they served him. Why?
Collect 12 valuable metal parts at the Western Outpost and bring them to Pin the Crafty at the Refuge.

A hero, you say? Have you ever expected this? Instead of fighting, Tep's hiding in a bunker like an ostrich burying its head in the sand! If he were an Imperial commander, it would have been regarded as a military crime. Well, luckily he's not, and we'll make use of all his abandoned infrastructure.
I heard that Sonin and Partisanov ordered to break the plant to pieces, so we'll make use of every single screw left! If you find something bigger or more valuable, lug it all here.
It looks like a useless rusty piece of metal, but it can save lives of the Resistance fighters. If you use it correctly...
How heavy they are! Oh, you're strong, aren't you?
Get to the Eastern Post and clear up the situation.
The console has only a few buttons and a couple of indicators on it. Looks like no big deal. Let's try activating the bridge and getting across...
What are you doing?! Get back to your cages, now! You have any idea who you're dealing with? I'm calling Grimnoth! Argh, Master, save me!
Disguised as a squirrel, get to the control console and disable the alarm, then open all the cages and release the captives.

Halsten! Halsten, brother, you're alive! I was afraid you'd been... Ha ha ha, I knew it! You can't kill a healer just like that!
We need to get out of here, brother. Take Gertrude and run, run for our lives. You see her? She's in one of the cages. We need to run... Shh! I have a plan!
Remember what they did to the poor Bully? Ha ha ha! They probably think because they skinned the squirrel, they killed her too... What those fools don't know is I saved her soul! It's here with me! The fight will go on!
Look, bro, we'll do it this way. I'll enter into a trance and turn you into our bully. I even have enough powers to make you invisible at times! Disguised as a squirrel, sneak past those frights to the control console by the stairs and disable the alarm. Then get back to the cages and unlock them. The cages are full of captives. Together, we'll show them!
A big escape! Enormous fuss! Ha ha ha!
Well done, bro! Make us proud! Did you happen to see Gertrude? She must be somewhere around, I'm telling you, I saw her...
Find the energy plant control console at the Eastern Post and break it down.

No, don't! Don't kill me! Whatever did I do, I just wanted to live, come on, don't, don't, please! I'll help you, just don't hurt me, argh! I know how to free the captives!
The Pyramid's not completed yet and the sarcophaguses are being stored outside, in the Spark Pen. The control console is outside too - it's here, behind the transformer tower. Breaking the console will disable the sarcophaguses and make the tower go kaboom! The explosion will be seen from the Refuge. Well, is my information valuable, eh? Can I rejoin the Resistance?
The Resistance is already here? Did the Light hear my prayers?
Stop, wait, what are you doing? Step away from the console! Who put you up to breaking it down? You're gonna kill all the captives!
Fight the Power Plant Guards to obtain 15 swords and bring them to Artem Sonin in the Refuge.

Halsten, bro, here's what I've been thinking about. What weapons does the Resistance have, sticks and stones? Meanwhile, did you see the swords the cultists have? Long and sharp! Remember them... Doing Gertrude and you... With a single swing... Well...
I mean it'd be nice to get a couple of these, eh? Let's collect some fifteen swords, take them to ours in the Refuge to arm them all! And then we'll do those cultists... Like they did you... With swords... Sharp as a razor...
A new weapon? I'll be damned! Few can stick their head into the devil's mouth and, beside returning alive, bring back a couple of fangs for souvenirs!

The swords are great, but there's something I don't like about them. Hold the grip. Can you feel it? That hardly audible whisper in your ears and dizziness... To hell with these swords. However, I appreciate your effort!
Kill the Power Plant Supervisor and take his tablet to Yasskul Nash.

My name is Yasskul Nash and I... I'm a coward. Also, I'm a senior power engineer and a slave to Tep, yet first of all, I'm a coward.
I didn't join the cult in search of eternal life. You see, our ZIT lab was shut down as unviable. I wanted to continue my research, and, when I was offered a "lab of my own as part of a private research project," I didn't hesitate to agree. When I understood what I'd agreed to, it was too late. There was no turning back.
There was a brave soul in our midst. Named Charles. He found out about the Resistance and planned an escape. I wanted to join him badly, but... I couldn't. On top of that, I came clean during an interrogation. Perhaps none of the escapers have survived because of my cowardice, and I... I'm sitting here and supplying power to the monster that ruined my nation. If the Resistance decides I deserve to die, I won't argue.
What? Charles is alive? That's a burden off my shoulders! Let's hurry to free your... Our! - brothers-in-arms.
After the illusory world was lost, the sarcophaguses have been working in a rough energy extraction mode. If we shut down the system, they're all will have their brains burned out! To keep them alive, we need to deactivate the system correctly. First, we need the access codes. My security clearance isn't enough for that, but there's a control room nearby. Bring me the supervisor's tablet and we'll be able to free all of the captive Sparks!
Some sold their souls to Tep in return for the promise of eternal life, others for divine power. While I, as it turns out, did it for a well-equipped lab and full social security!
The control codes? Excellent! Now we can cut off power to the Pyramid.
Shut off 6 valves at the foot of the tower and report to Yasskul Nash.

Just a minute... Wait... Uh-huh, uh-huh... Whatever is that... May the devil take it all!
No, don't worry, there's nothing to be afraid of. One of the processes crashed and we're gonna have to shut down manually. Would you mind shutting off a few valves? They are not longer marching, there are six of them, and they're all located in the basement of the transformer tower. Go shut them off, will you? And stay sharp, the place is guarded heavily!
Whoever wrote all this? However did Tep expect to conquer the entire Sarnaut with computers crashing after every sneeze?
Ready! I'm on it... Keep your fingers crossed! If the next process crashes, we'll have to get to the top of the tower!
Use the reprogramming device to hack 6 Tep's Mechanoids and report to Yasskul Nash.

While I'm fiddling with the control program, try out this device. I knocked it off when we were planning an escape, but I never gave it to Charles. Now it's gonna help us gain some time.
This is a reprogramming device, it resets the friend-or-foe system in mechanoids so they take friendly units for targets and the other way around. You don't have to understand anything: aim the device, push the button and enjoy gladiator-style battle. While the machines fight each other, they will ignore us.
Be careful, though: I assembled the device from stolen parts using makeshift tools and driven by enthusiasm, so failure is an option.
Well... Uh-huh... What is that "invalid field value"?... Listen, do me a favor, stop hovering over my shoulder. I'll do my part, and you take care of the mechanoids.
It's surely running already: the howling and clanking is heard all over the island. And I'm almost through with the freaking code.
Find the June Ruins in the Spark Pen and check if they are functional.

It's done. I cut off power supply to the captives, so the machines stopped sucking the light of their Sparks. We can free the captives without risk of injury. Unfortunately, everyone can't be awakened automatically: the sarcophaguses were designed with a thought of holding their contents forever. However, this can be done by your brothers-in-arms. For you, there's a task of greater importance: someone has to prepare a secure retreat route. Rushing across the bridge with a crowd of weakened captives is not the best idea.
I saw a familiar thing in the Spark Pen: something very similar to the June ruins. I couldn't check if they were operational, but if they are, we're saved: powered by the Adventurer's Stones, they'll move us directly to the Refuge while Tep's servants won't be able to pursue us!
I'm going to join the rebels, and you go look for the ruins. If everything goes smooth... I hope I'll have a chance to personally beg Charles his forgiveness.
The ancient ruins of the June Portal are still filled with magical powers... Or, to be more precise, there's still a kindling of them in there.
A glow is rising from the core of the crystal... The ruins are coming back to life!
Fight Tep Cultists and Sacrificers in the Spark Pen to collect 10 fragments of the June Crystal. Restore the crystal and use it to fix the June Ruins.

The Ruins are hardly responding to your Adventurer's Stone. Little wonder: someone broke a huge crystal out of the very core. Looks like you'll have to find another way... Wait, what are those shiny things hanging around the cultists' necks? They broke the June crystal to make jewelry out of the fragments!
I wonder if the shattered crystal can be fixed. And how can we be sure you won't get teleported straight to Kyoltmark or beyond? The risk is high... Yet staying here, amidst a whole army of Tep's servants, is even riskier!
The ruins are critically damaged, and their magic has no effect.

There you are! Well, report on the job you did! Don't know what you were facing, but the result is obvious: across all fronts, the cultists are retreating to the Pyramid. Perhaps we don't have to expect another attack on the Refuge.
Get back to the illusory world and talk to the Pudgy Family in the League Settlement.

That orb of invisibility is lovely. It's a pity the Imperial commanders are more scared of their internal security than they are of Tep: we could have saved plenty of time and effort if we had gotten this thing sooner! However, let's be grateful to them for having it in the first place. By using it as a cover, we'll be able to scout the most remote isles and prepare acts of sabotage right under Tep's nose!
However, we'll do that by ourselves: for you, there's a matter of greater importance. Charles and I thought about what the Ghost had said and we concluded he was right. If we find the core of illusion, we'll be able to make Tep lose control over the illusory world that is his main source of power! Yet where can we find that core... Our brothers-in-arms found nothing for now, yet our time is running out. Go back to the world of daydreaming and help them. Find the Pudgy Family, they'll explain the situation. And while you search through the illusory Irdrich, we'll try gaining some extra time for you by causing Tep as much trouble as we can on the real Irdrich.
Reinforcements from the real world? Great!
Meet with Spike the Forester at the Dump.

There's two pieces of news for you, good and bad, as usual. The bad news is that Tep has finally understood he is fighting a strong army, not catlings. So the outposts are reinforced, and his sentries search for the Refuge day and night.
The good news is about the documents from the captain's safe. We found out that this is a technical manual for an invention with a hard-to-utter name. I call it the Orb of Invisibility, a concealing mechanism capable to make the entire detachment invisible! The only device was stored on the Imperial ship, Vlad, whose wreckage can be found at the Damp. We have already sent Spike the Forrester there to inspect them. Speak with her, and I hope you'll manage to find that Orb.

Here comes my help! Nice, yep! Let's get to work, frittering away the Imperial treasure! Suppose, Partisanov will be commended by Aidenus. And we will be asked by Rysina about the secret scraps fallen into hands of the League jerks? We better win, as success is never blamed, yep. And if we lose, there will be no one to blame, either way!
Go back to the Illusory World and talk to Yasskul Tikhti at the Imperial Outpost.

That orb of invisibility is lovely. It's a pity the Imperial commanders are more scared of their internal security than they are of Tep: we could have saved plenty of time and effort if we had had this thing earlier! However, let's be grateful to them for having it in the first place. By using it as a cover, we'll be able to scout the most remote isles and prepare acts of sabotage right under Tep's nose!
However, we'll do that by ourselves: for you, there's a matter of greater importance. Charles and I thought about what the Ghost had said and we concluded he was right. If we find the core of illusion, we'll be able to make Tep lose control over the illusory world that is his main source of power! Yet where can we find that core... Our brothers-in-arms found nothing for now, yet our time is running out. Go back to the world of daydreaming and help them. Find the Yasskul Tikhti, he'll explain the situation. And while you search through the illusory Irdrich, we'll try gaining some extra time for you by causing Tep as much trouble as we can on the real Irdrich.
Reinforcements from the real world? How opportune.
That island name Marai-Nui, you call it Crystal Mountain. It is taboo. You better not go there, not look, not even think. Ulumi Half-Wing broke the taboo once, flew there, and look at him now!
h: Ask about the mountain in the north

t: Obtain 10 cutters and 10 mana batteries on the dump and bring them to Pin the Crafty in the Rebel Refuge.

When the troops are cut off from the supplies, they have a several options. We're not looking into the lie-down-and-croak scenario. Normally, one would force one's way to the friendlies, but that's not an option in our case. All we can do is: find ways to become self-supporting, preferably at the enemy's expense. That's what we're gonna do.
First, we need a tool. Second, we need power supply for that tool. We'll have to haul all that from the dump. That's what we call the isle beyond the Ship Graveyard: Tep knows about it, but it looks like a dump. There are rusty cripples - we call them garbage collectors - wandering around the place. These are armed with valuable cutters. That's our first priority. The job is simple: charge, knock out, take off the cutter. As a second priority, the dump has lots of damaged ship equipment where you can find a pile of batteries. Bringing ten pieces of each would be enough to reinforce our defenses!
This dump is actually a fount of useful stuff. I wish I could carry it all at once.
Perfect. Attach one to the other, and you're set. You can shred iron... or cultists. Self-support in action, heh!
Kill the Cultist Overseers and talk to Fleur de Ardeur. Report your success to Spike the Forester.

Damn, that was a ship! The terror of the Astral and the pride of the fleet! Bang - and there you go - our Vlad is reduced to a pile of scrap. But in addition to the ship's collapse, some terrible filth settled down in its remains. Like a dragon, but not actually one - a huge three-headed flying lizard. The cultists take their captives to it, and it gorges on them. While that scary freak is in the ship, we can't expect to get the magic device.
Look, look, here they are! Another victim they brought him for dinner. We need... Oh, damn it, that's an elf! Let's just leave her to hell here, eh?
No, sorry. I said that without thinking. Of course, we have to save her. Can you handle it?
My fists clench every time I see an elf... But I can't leave her here for the serpent to feast on!
Well, you saved an elf. Another week among mechanoids, and I'll probably go drinking with gibberlings.
Kill 8 Tep's Hounds at the Dump and report to Fleur de Ardeur.

Wow... Let me catch my breath... I don't know how to thank you. They... They didn't just want to kill me! That three-headed monster... It devours both your flesh and your Spark! Well... That can't be undone!
I've been in captivity before... I thought the worst thing was orcs' ridicule and mockery. But those cultists... They're not people any more. I don't know what they believe in, but my stomach turns upside down every time I hear their voices. Let's leave this place fast!
No, no, wait, wait, we need to stay calm. We need... We need to be reasonable. They have a whole pack of mechanical hounds. If we run now, our tracks will lead them straight to the Refuge. Please break them apart. And then we'll run!
Come on, hurry! Light forbid, the cultists may come back!
You did a hell of a job! Nuts and bolts were flying everywhere! That's impressive!
Kill the Cultist Tyrant, take the traveling bag and bring it back to Fleur de Ardeur.

Does the Resistance truly exist? The captives were whispering about it, but I wouldn't dare believe it. If it all consists of heroes like you, Tep has no chance! Come on, show me the way to the Refuge fast!
But no, wait! I'm a doctor, you see, and I believe my knowledge can be of use to the Resistance. But those brutes took my instruments, and I'm no good without them! Do me a favor, bring back my traveling bag. I saw it taken by that cultist, the tyrant, supervisor of the prison wardens, the most cruel one. Go kick his filthy ass!
I hope he didn't lay his filthy hands on my instruments!

Thank you! Well, well... Looks like everything is in place... Oh no! My favorite scalpel is gone! Oh, it could be a dangerous weapon in a prentice hand... So we must be careful.
You say, the Refuge is over there, at the southern part of the allod. Well, I think I will be able to find my way there. Thank you!
Obtain 10 chain Fragments from piles of garbage at the Dump and bring them to Spike the Forester.

Well, the lunch is gone, and the eater is about to show up. Listen, I have an idea! Let's make a trap for the serpent! You know how we'd catch drakes on Yazes Shard? No? I'll show you.
First, we need some chains. And not just any chains, but adamantite ones: this beast can't be restrained by iron or mithril. As it happens, chains are in rich supply here. Go find me some ten chains among that junk, the longer the better.
We'd often tie up drakes with ropes, but to that monster, ropes are like spider web.
Uh-huh! Nice chains. These can be used to tie up an Octulhu, let alone a serpent!
Put on rags and lure the serpent. When it shows up, cast a net over it and defeat it.

Here, the net is ready. What do you think? A freaking piece of handicraft! Listen up, here's what we're gonna do.
You're stronger than me, so you'll do the more dangerous part. You'll be the bait - sorry, but it'll swallow me without even noticing. Take this net and put on these rags - Nezeb forbid, the serpent may spot the trap. Put them on. Once we whack Tep and get back home, we'll wear better clothes.
Then go to the post and wait for the serpent. Pretend you're a victim. Once it comes flying, cast the net. It'll get entangled in the net, and we'll kick its ass. Is the plan OK? Let's get down to it.
Don't be scared: it worked with drakes, it will work with the three-headed freak too.

Damn it! We almost got it! I just didn't have time to check all the knots on the net, or we'd be cooking barbecue with the serpent's flesh.
Well, screw it. It won't escape next time. It fled from the ship, that's the main thing. Let's go rummage through the scrap!
Take the orb of invisibility from the chest in the ruins of the Imperial flagship and bring it to Gleb Partisanov in the Refuge.
Finally, we can take the orb. It'll be funny as hell if we find out it has been damaged in the wreck, eh?
How's your search? Did you find the device?

That's the thing! First, the astral stabilizer and the explosives, now the orb of invisibility... I wonder what else the Empire has in stock! Maybe if we carefully search through the holds, we'll find a device with the only button on it that reads, "Kill them all"?
Kill 10 baby serpents at the Dump and report to Spike the Forester.

An interesting question: three-headed serpents, how do they propagate? I'm not asking just for fun! We couldn't handle one, but what if there's gonna be a whole pack? There's a nest full of baby serpents nearby. Well, they may be babies compared to that serpent, but they can swallow a gibberling whole. They are looked after and fed by the cultists... What if they grow as big as their parent? Whack them all while they are relatively small.
I remember some poem from my childhood, like, "For a baby serpent, a snaky life is certain"... Hey, what's so funny?
Whack the suckers! I wonder if their flesh is poisonous! Serpent flesh will taste delicious after a mushroom diet!
Collect 5 Ship Cannon Parts, 5 Ship Shield parts and 10 Fragments of Rigging on the Ship Graveyard and bring them to Pin the Crafty at the Rebel Refuge.

You know what a soldier's practicality is? First, it's knowing what and where can be stolen without being noticed. Second, the ability to assemble something useful from useless junk, he he. Without being practical, you can't survive on these rocks, may the devil take them. For we got nothing but all sorts of trash, fragments and shards here, and even those must be hauled carefully in order not to expose the base. They'll spot us sooner or later, that's for sure, but the later the better. Until they haven't, we need to pile up energy and supplies.
The entire Irdrich is a big ship graveyard, but the isle to the east of ours has them in especially rich supply and, most importantly, they're not all rotten yet. Go rummage through the remains. Pull a crystal from a cannon, a battery from a shield... This way, we can reinforce our defenses. Is the task clear? Then go!
The mages are still researching if they can get something out of nothing. The adjutant's job is more difficult: how to assemble something from heck knows what, he he he!
Incredible. Back in Nezebgrad, we'd write it off as scrap right away, but here, every chip is a treasure. Here, take your reward. Amazing stuff.
Explore the cliffs next to the Refuge. Fight the Clanking Warriors to obtain 10 parts and bring them to Artem Sonin.

The threat is over, so you can come out and look around. Be careful, though: don't lead another squad here. Walk around the Refuge. You can visit the neighboring isles, too.
And for you to not just stroll around idly, I have a job for you. To fight your enemy, you need to know them both inside and out. Tep has some new kind of mechanized undead here. Horrible units with rotting flesh built into them, bah! Disassemble ten of them and bring me their parts for research. You'll learn to know them and we, Light willing, will find out something new.
But stay sharp and on your guard. A weird place - Tep knows what can happen here.
Do you like the landscape? There was a time when it was exactly like the illusory world.
Those are horrible things! The ones you'd hate to touch. Never mind, we'll research them and find out the best way to whack that filth.
Check if any of the fugitives survived, exterminate the squad of Tep's servants along with their leader, and report to Charles de Doucer in the Ship Graveyard.

Gosh... I barely escaped. A few more minutes and my remains would have been scattered as far as Tep's strongholds. Thank you!
My name is Charles de Doucer. My friends and I escaped and hid among the remains of the ships, but they tracked us. The battle was brief. I fled, but I couldn't get far. If it weren't for you, that would have been the end of me.
Sorry for asking you to risk your life, but I'm no fighter. Please go to that ship and take a look: maybe some of ours survived. If Tep's servants are still there... I think you'll handle them. Be careful, though: that's an elite squad after all!
I hope some of ours are still alive.

So they're all dead... Well then. Nothing we can do. We all knew the risks.
Wait, wait, describe that elf in more detail... Whoa! You have any idea who she was? Nihil, one of Tep's close acolytes and a genuine inventor. She had her hand in everything running and creeping around here. A scary woman... Praise be to the Light that the cultists don't resurrect!
Escort Charles de Doucer to the Refuge.

That's it. I'm left alone. Friends killed, shelter destroyed, nowhere left to go. I wonder how long I'll last this way. Have you been at large for long? How do you manage to survive?
What? The Resistance? Praise be to the Light. Say, is there any chance you need mechanics down there? I can handle all kinds of tools and I'm good at building and repairing. If there's a chance, if only a delusive one, to overthrow Tep, I want to have a hand in it.
However, I'm no good as a warrior, and I have nowhere to go. Will you see me off as far as the Rebel Refuge?
Charles de Doucer? Hmm. OK, let's watch that de Doucer. We need mechanics badly. But I don't like his last name!
Show Charles de Doucer's letter to Artem Sonin in the Refuge.

How strange! The only bodies found next to the ship were those of Tep's cultists. One of them had a letter in his pocket that you found... It was signed by Charles de Doucer! This is so suspicious that perhaps the privacy of correspondence may be violated...
Well, that's disappointing. The characters in the letter look familiar, but not the language. There's a plan in the letter, though: some carelessly sketched corridors and arrows. Looks like this is an escape plan indeed... But where from, exactly? This find should be shown to the rebels' leader.
Charles de Doucer? Never heard of him before. Where is he?
So this was in a dead cultist's pocket? I wonder where they escaped from. There's nothing like this plan near the sarcophaguses. It's as suspicious as it gets...

I don't like that Charles. He doesn't look like a miserable victim of Tep's: he's too well-fed and well-groomed. And this letter... Could he be a snake in the grass? Go conduct a forced interrogation: find out who he is, where he's from, how he fell into Tep's clutches and how he escaped. If you catch him lying, take him to the edge of the allod and push him into the Astral. The last thing we need is leading a spy to the Refuge!
So, have you researched the background of our new ally?

Is that the way it is? One who betrays once will betray again. On the other hand, the knowledge this turncoat has can come in quite useful.
Well then, we'll watch him. You'll do it because that winged smartass owes his life to you. Go find out how he can help us.
Excellent! Perfect! I'll prepare your ship in 5 minutes.
h: Give away the License and 1500 gold to receive an Astral Ship
Give away the License and 1500 gold to receive an Astral Ship

t: What do you want to know?
Perfect! I'll make arrangements to start the construction right away. It's quite a long process, but I can tell you how to speed it up.
h: Pay 1500 gold to start the construction of your ship.
Pay 1500 gold to start the construction of your ship.

t: Find the skeleton of the Imperial ship Chimera at the Dump.

I recalled an important thing. The captain of one of the Imperial ships had memorized data on the prototype of an experimental device that allowed distortions to be stabilized in deep layers of the Astral. Regretfully, when I found out about that, it was too late: the ship was sent to the Dump and there was no time retrieve it... But wait, why regret it? That was fortunate: the last thing we need is that technology in the hands of Tep! Thanks to my then negligence: if the device is intact, it can come in very useful.
I'm not sure where exactly the ship's remains are, but I remember the name: "Chimera." Try finding it. It will be very unfortunate if some of the engineers still loyal to Tep decide to correct my mistake. If you find the device, bring it to the Buzzing Family. They're good craftsmen and they're League citizens. Despite the war against Tep, entrusting this to an Imperial scientist would mean getting him court-martialed.
A burnt board with blackened golden letters on it is protruding from a pile of garbage and fragments. "Chimera." Here it is, the ship Charles was talking about!
Fight the garbage collectors at the Dump to obtain 20 parts of the device and bring them to the Buzzing Family in the Refuge.

Damn it! Garbage collectors already got their hands on the ship and disassembled it to parts. Even if the device was here, it turned into building materials for Tep's construction works.
However... Maybe not all is lost yet! The device was kept in the depths of the ship, and it was only a while ago that metal pincers found it. You need to shake down the local trash collectors: maybe they didn't take the parts far.
Nice parts! Only there are few of them. You sure it's all there was?
Amazing. Are those Imperials smart or what! It's a pity the iron dummies destroyed such beauty. We can't promise anything, but we'll try fixing it.

Fight Mechanoids to collect 10 high-powered batteries and install them on the small boat. Fly through several anomalies and use the Experimental Stabilizer to destroy them, then return to the Buzzing Family.

It's done. Good as new! Well, almost. I had to weld it here, glue it there... We're almost sure it works exactly the way it should!
We'll explain how to use it. A while ago, new Wormholes to undiscovered layers of the Astral appeared. Can you imagine how enthusiastic the headquarters of both the League and the Empire grew? New opportunities, new islands, new treasures! Only they couldn't reach them: these Wormholes are so polluted with anomalies that any probe gets tied in a knot. A new race began: who'll be the first to invent a device that would stabilize the Astral. As you can see, the Empire has won... though Chimera's crew didn't have enough time to properly test it.
There are lots of such anomalies around Irdrich. We've prepared a small boat - it's frayed, but it will work for a while. However, we don't have any batteries to install on it. There's a lot of old bangers around here, you may get a few batteries from them. Start the engine and approach an anomaly. The device must neutralize it. If everything runs smooth, the way into new astral layers will be open!
If the device works, we're in for a gold rush. Can you imagine everyone racing one another into that new layer? And what if there's nothing there, he he he!
It works... We can't believe it, it works! Now let's take care of Tep quick so we can get our hands on the treasures of the deep Astral!
Talk to Alexandra Soldina at the port.

Oh, those mercenaries! Are they shrewd! No sooner were the device blueprints made public than a crowd of greenhorn Novices rushed into the new Astral layer, though they had no navigation experience whatever, let alone in the old layers. And while their Sparks were taking a breather in the Purgatory, the mercenaries flew their ships there and arranged flights for Novices supervised by experienced astral aces. They're cultivating both their customer base and a replacement generation. What about you, have you got the guys to fly? If so, talk to Alexandra Soldina, she'll tell you everything.

We never run out of customers ever since we got this miracle of an astral machine. We hardly have time to stuff our pockets with gold! What, you also want to lay your hands on treasures of the new layer? Then listen up.
Talk to Vlastemir Naymitov at the port.

Oh, those mercenaries! Are they shrewd! No sooner were the device blueprints made public than a crowd of greenhorn Novices rushed into the new Astral layer, though they had no navigation experience whatever, let alone in the old layers. And while their Sparks were taking a breather in the Purgatory, the mercenaries flew their ships there and arranged flights for Novices supervised by experienced astral aces. They're cultivating both their customer base and a replacement generation. What about you, have you got the guys to fly? If so, talk to Vlastemir Naymitov, he'll tell you everything.

We never run out of customers ever since we got this miracle of an astral machine. We hardly have time to stuff our pockets with gold! What, you also want to lay your hands on treasures of the new layer? Then listen up.
Collect a Bottle of Sea Water, an Aviak's Feather, a Tropical Flower and a Fragment of Crystal Guard in the illusory world and bring them to Klavdia Kalugina in the Rebel Refuge of the real world.

Charles and I have studied the cultitsts' sparks. They are... Weird. Tep has changed them. We have already seen the monsters eating the sparks, yet this is something different. Looks like he deprived them of reality making merely parts of an immense dream. What do the cultists see when they fight or work for Tep? One can only guess. The illusory world is Tep's experiment, and he's not only trying to become god, he strives for making Sarnaut part of his dream!
Fortunately, this experiment is now in our hands. Tep is a creator by nature, or an artist I would say. He puts his heart into everything he creates. This will help us to break the continuity of the great dream, that started there, on illusory Irdrich.
I can make a thing that will protect you from Tep. We'll use the stuff from the wordl of illusions, all bearing imprints of Tep's soul. Let's see, a bottle with sea water, an aviak's feather, a tropical flower, a fragment of Crystal Guard. That's all.
We consider Tep a monster, a villain and a murderer. Well, he probably sees us as barbarians not able to understand the genuine art. Or he's very likely to consider us a snack.

Can you imagine that this bright feather, and this shining crystal, and this beautiful flower are all clones of Tep's soul! It's hard to believe, yet to understand it is the only way to defeat the enemy!
Drink a potion with a glare of Tep's spark.

I've finished. I bet you have never drunk such a muck! Sorry, it's absolutely necessary, if you want to overcome Tep.
This potion contains the very essence of the illusory world, a distilled glare of Tep's Spark. It will make you see what's inside your enemy, make you understand him. You know, Tep's like a god with his strongest armor and sharpest weapon, and the most powerful magic that one can imagine. Your only chance to win is to feel this from the source.
If I had a choice I wouldn't dip into that abyss. However, I had to, and I had a drink... and I'm still alive.

Hush, hush.. It's all over. I was afraid you would turn gray. What you've seen is the real Tep. That is your enemy. Now his most wicked witchcraft will be helpless against you, though some of them still pose danger.
Enter Tep's Pyramid and kill Key-Keeper and his servant, Bouncer.

It's time to make our final spurt. Tep's forces are crushed down, the remaining cultists and mechanoids drop back inside the Pyramid. It's a perfect chance for us! We have a single attempt to defeat Tep, or the whole world will turn into a tremendous burial ground.
Here's the plan: we should form two detachments. I will lead soldiers to fight Tep's main forces, while assault troops headed by you will penetrate into the Pyramid to kill Tep.
There's one more thing you should know: Klavdia decided to join the fight. Though she helped us to get out of sarcophaguses, I wouldn't completely trust her. She will meet your detachment after you defeat the guards and the Key-Keeper.
Unfortunately, we have no Pyramid's outline and only scarce pieces of information about the enemy's forces, so you should act as you see fit.
Is the task clear? Ok, let's do it. And may Tensess help us!
There you are at last! I started worrying!

Are you surprised by seeing me here? I used the orb of invisibility, of course. I've changed it a little bit, so that now it cannot hide a party of militarymen, but perfectly conceals a young lady, just like me.
OK, let me put you in the picture. Tep's den is in the upper part of the Pyramid, just beneath the spire. There are two ways that can bring you there, either through the laboratory or the control center. Whatever way you choose, you'll have to fight with the enemy waiting for you. So decide who you want to defeat more, a master of illusions or an expert in magic engineering?
Kill Sihal and meet with Klavdia Kalugina at the lift that will bring you to the top of the Pyramid.

Sihal... My knowledge of him is rather slight, though it's enough to make me filled with loathing.
Do you remember the pestilent shadows on the Wandering Isle? Ugh, disgusting... How could anyone agree to let such a monster live inside his body! Sihal did it. He's a close acolyte of Tep, and the only likely reason for the Arisen to contact a spark devourer is that Tep's madness is contagious.
Sihal is half an Arisen and half a pestilent shadow. He's a terrible and dangerous monster. A reckless mind of a Zem scientist amplified by the unknown shadowy magic made him capable of controlling an entire world of illusions. You overcame Sihal once, in the Crystal Palace. He's enraged by his defeat, and anger gives him power, and there are myriads of shadows around protecting their master. I must confess that I shudder with fear, as our world has never faced such horrendous evil. May you succeed in your fight to shelter us from it!
Your victory will ultimately break all the connections between the real and the illusory worlds, and we will be able to free all the captives. The lives of people and the fate of the world is at stake!
The victory is now so close. The final step is to get to the very top of the Pyramid and defeat its owner.
What a fight!.. Who would have thought that Sihal was that strong!
Defeat Nihil and meet with Klavdia Kalugina at the lift that will bring you to the top of the Pyramid.

Does the name of Celestine de Ardeur means anything for you? No? Yet it should have. As she dreams of revenging herself upon you.
It's because of you she became a cripple confined to the Pyramid forever. Isn't it a sad destiny? Though she fully deserved that...
You know her as Nihil, a fierce servant of Tep. You fought with her to save the life of Charles de Doucer, a mechanic, amidst the astral ship wreckage. Yet I remember her as a young and enthusiastic Elven girl. Simeon de Ardeur expected her to have a great future! Well, it can be called great but not in Elven terms.
I can even guess how Tep managed to win Celestine. She has been interested in machines and devices, and Tep, despite his madness, is the best engineer ever. A genius!
Celestine was a brilliant inventor. It was she who created Caesaria, an artificial intelligence controlling the Darkblood Citadel. Now Nihil has become an artificial mind herself.
Tep has thought up a stiff punishment for her defeat. You know that cultists cannot revive, but Tep's able to return a spark into a dead body. That's what he did to Celestine! He returned Nihil to life, if her miserable existence can be called life... Tep has integrated the body of his disgraced servant into the Pyramid control mechanisms making Nihil his devoted watchdog. Can you imagine how she must be suffering, having lost the very notion of beauty.
If you can understand this, please make her death as less painful possible. I feel sorry for her. No one deserves such a destiny...
You wouldn't wish it on your worst enemy, to be confined to your creation and watch its downfall...

Finally Nihil can rest in peace... I wish I could have brought her to reason after defeat. Celestine's brilliant mind could have done many good things for the sake of beauty. What is done cannot be undone. Now you should go right to the enemy's den and eliminate this threat to the world.
Reach the top of Tep's Pyramid and survive the attacks of the lift keepers.

It has been a long and risky march, yet now the victory is close at hand. All you have to do is to go upwards, to the top of the Pyramid, and fight Tep. This would be a fabulous battle, and you just have to win and save the world!
My heart is full of misgivings. The lift is the only way to get to the top, which makes it the best place for ambush. I feel the enemy will strike as soon as you get there! I should come first. I have my own tricks so I will be there before you. If there's an ambush as we expect I' ll draw them away. It's not a big deal for a child of God, after all!
When moving upwards, please stay alert. Tep has set his toy dragon loose, the one you fought with earlier. The danger's lurking around you.
Wish me good luck. See you soon at the top of the Pyramid!
Looks like I was under a delusion as to my divine powers. I can't believe they knocked me out so easily!

Tep is so smart, he knew I would be the first to get here, and that ambush was waiting for me, not you. He planned that three-headed monster would destroy you when you were moving upwards. And he wanted to catch me alive! Luckily, his plan failed.
Oh, with these wounds I cannot help you in the next battle... It hurts so bad!

Hurry! I could divert the cultists by arranging a few small but highly amusing accidents. Watching the cultists scatter from the frenzied mechanoids is such fun! It's a pity, though, they'll soon figure out what's what and come here en masse. You have very little time.
No, I'm not going with you. Frail girls like me have nothing to do with all that cold steel you love to brandish so much. Besides, I had a hard enough time of it already. The damned fanatics haven't a clue how to treat women, not even the simplest rules about not hitting them. Apparently, I made them really mad, he-he!
So go on and don't you dare croak shamefully! I spent too much time and effort on this world for some crazy old freak to turn it into a mass grave!
Freedom! Finally, I'm free again! My body may be ruined, but my spirit is stronger than ever!
Damned Tep! Our great astral campaign resulted in zilch and, to make matters worse, we couldn't die a proper death either. Years of captivity spent in that pyramid seemed like an eternity to me!

Hurry! I could divert the cultists by arranging a few small but highly amusing accidents. Watching the cultists scatter from the frenzied mechanoids is such fun! It's a pity, though, they'll soon figure out what's what and come here en masse. You have very little time.
No, I'm not going with you. Frail girls like me have nothing to do with all that cold steel you love to brandish so much. Besides, I had a hard enough time of it already. The damned fanatics haven't a clue how to treat women, not even the simplest rules about not hitting them. Apparently, I made them really mad, he-he!
So go on and don't you dare croak shamefully! I spent too much time and effort on this world for some crazy old freak to turn it into a mass grave!
Light... Sounds... Life... I haven't seen all this in such a long time!

Don't be afraid of me. I am a captive of Tep's, just like the many prisoners of this pyramid. I already had to spend a few years bound by a powerful spell once, yet that was nothing compared to the absolute power the mad warlock has over the defenseless Sparks!
